concerns.text: Task T008 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it writes `model_primary.pt` and `model_primary.json`, which are consumed by later tasks (T009, T010, T011, T013). The existence of this consumer creates an implicit ordering requirement, so T008 is not truly parallel‑safe.

Task T009 is also marked `[P]` yet it reads the model checkpoint produced by T008 and writes `validation_report.json`, which is a required input for T010, T011, and T013. This dependency makes parallel execution unsafe.

Task T010 carries `[P]` but updates `validation_report.json` in‑place after reading it. Concurrent execution with any task that reads the same JSON (e.g., T011) would cause race conditions; thus the `[P]` tag is inaccurate.

Task T011 is marked `[P]` yet it depends on the fully‑populated `validation_report.json` and `sensitivity_sweep.csv`. Running it in parallel with tasks that modify those files would break reproducibility.
Task T012 is a driver script that sequentially invokes all previous tasks. Marking it `[P]` contradicts its purpose; it cannot be safely run in parallel with any other task.

Task T013 is tagged `[P]` but reads `validation_report.json`, `report.html`, and model/dataset artifacts produced by earlier tasks. Parallel execution could read incomplete artifacts, violating data‑flow ordering.

Task T014 adds unit‑ and integration‑tests for all scripts. While tests themselves are read‑only, the task’s purpose is to validate the entire pipeline after all artifacts exist, so it should not be marked `[P]` as it implicitly depends on the completion of every prior task.

User Story 2 (US2) tasks (T006–T014) are not independently shippable because they depend on the filtered dataset produced in US1 (tasks T001–T005). The spec‑kit precedent requires each US block to be testable end‑to‑end on its own; US2 violates this by lacking its own data‑acquisition steps.
